title: Why Can't You Raise Just ONE Finger? ☝️
description:
Try it: make a fist and raise only your middle finger, all the way up. Did your ring finger come up too? The cords that lift your fingers run over the back of your hand, and little bands tie them together (here they're handcuffs). The ring finger's cord is tied to BOTH of its neighbours, so it drags them along, and they drag it: that's why the ring finger is the worst of all at moving alone. A perfect one takes practice. The composer Robert Schumann built a gadget to train his middle finger in the 1830s, the finger went stiff, and he never played concerts again. Whether the gadget did it, historians still argue. Did your ring finger rise? Yes or no?
